brief: RBC's July tracker estimates global active datacenter development at approximately 66 GW, up 21 GW versus March 2026, and planned/potential third-party capacity above 304 GW, up 36 GW. Growth is driven mainly by the Americas, where under-construction capacity rose from 26.8 GW to 45.8 GW, led by Texas. The top 4 hyperscalers hold a combined 16.8 GW under construction and 39.6 GW planned; Amazon leads the planned pipeline at 17.3 GW, while Meta and Microsoft lead under-construction activity, aided by Microsoft re-mobilizing previously paused Ohio and North Carolina campuses. Behind-the-meter power strategies cover 16% of tracked projects (24% in North America), led by gas co-location. Liquid cooling is being reframed as a compute-efficiency lever rather than infrastructure overhead. Development faces rising headwinds: project withdrawals and moratoria accelerated April-June 2026, capped by New York's Executive Order 62 (July 22), which freezes permitting above 50MW and shifts grid-upgrade costs from ratepayers to developers. RBC identifies contagion to Virginia and Texas as the mispriced risk if either adopts the same cost-allocation framework, since already-permitted projects are shielded but discretionary-stage projects face an uncapped one-year-plus timeline.
